data.name: Darius
data.gender_notes: Darius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word 'dara' meaning 'man' and the suffix 'ius' meaning 'god' or 'king'. In the Bible, Darius is the name of two kings: King Darius the Great of Persia (522–486 BC) and King Darius I of Persia (521–486 BC). Darius is also the name of a martyr from the early Christian church. The name Darius carries the meaning “Man, Lord, God, King” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Darius usually hope their child will grow to embody man, lord, god, king and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes godly leadership and obedience to the will of God.
data.etymology: Darius belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man, Lord, God, King.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darius total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: דאריוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דאריוס הוא שם פרסי שמשמעותו 'המלך', 'השושיל', 'הנשיא', או 'האחראי'. השם נגזר מהשורש הפרסי 'דר' שפירושו 'להחזיק' או 'לקיים'. בתקופה הפרסית, השם דאריוס היה שמץ נפוץ בקרב המלכים והאצילים. באסלאם וביהדות, השם דאריוס מוזכר בקוראן ובתנ'ך, בהתאמה, כמלך פרס חשוב.

in_greek.name: Δαρείος
in_greek.meaning: ο βασιλιάς, ο ηγέτης, ο άρχων
in_greek.long_meaning: Δαρείος είναι ένα Περσικό όνομα που σημαίνει 'ο βασιλιάς', 'ο ηγέτης', 'ο άρχων'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από το Περσικό ρίζα 'dar' που σημαίνει 'να κρατάω' ή 'να διατηρώ'. Στον αρχαίο κόσμο, το όνομα Δαρείος ήταν διάσημο ανάμεσα στους Πέρσες βασιλιάδες και ευγενείς. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη και στην Ιστορία της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Δαρείος αναφέρεται ως σύμβολο δύναμης και ηγεσίας.

in_latin.name: Darius
in_latin.long_meaning: Darius is a Persian name meaning 'king', 'ruler', 'leader', or 'governor'. Derived from the Persian root 'dar', which means 'to hold' or 'to maintain'. Historically, the name Darius was prominent among Persian monarchs and nobles. In Christian tradition, the name Darius symbolizes authority, leadership, and power.

in_english.name: Darius
in_english.meaning: a kingly or noble name, symbolizing leadership and power
in_english.long_meaning: The name Darius originates from the Persian Empire, meaning 'he who holds firm the good' or 'the king'. Derived from the Old Persian name 'Dārayavahu', which is composed of 'dāraya', meaning 'to hold' or 'to keep', and 'vahu', meaning 'good'. Historically, Darius I and Darius II were notable kings of Persia. In the Bible, Darius is mentioned in the book of Ezra and Nehemiah as a king of Persia who allowed the Jews to rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem. The name Darius conveys strength, courage, and leadership, making it a popular choice for Christian parents seeking a name with rich history and spiritual significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Darius carries a rich cultural significance, being directly linked to ancient Persian history. Darius was the name of two powerful and esteemed kings of Persia. Their rule marked significant changes and achievements in Persian history, including religious and territorial expansion, as well as advancements in science, technology, and the arts. The name Darius continues to evoke a sense of nobility, power, and wisdom, reflecting the majesty and grandeur of the wealthy Persian Empire.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Darius holds a special spiritual meaning as it is also the name of a martyr from the early Christian church. The story of Darius, as it is retold in legends and hagiographies, emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith in the face of adversity and persecution. Darius' courage and commitment to his beliefs serve as inspiring examples for generations of Christians, reminding us of the inherent strength and resilience that comes from living our faith authentically.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Darius represents courage and divine guidance, symbolizing a leader who relies on faith and strength in God during times of adversity. The name echoes the biblical King Darius, known for his wisdom, power, and compassion.

biblical_reference.note: Darius I, king of Persia, allowed the Jews to rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem (Ezra 6:1-12)

historical_references.reference: Darius I, also known as Darius the Great, reigned from 522 to 486 BCE as king of the Achaemenid Empire, which included present-day Iran and parts of Central Asia, Egypt, and the Balkans. He is famous for defeating the invading army of Xerxes I and halting the Greek advance into the Persian Empire.
historical_references.context: Achaemenid Empire, Persia, Greece, Xerxes I

historical_references.reference: Darius III, who ruled from 336 to 330 BCE, was the last king of the Achaemenid Empire. He faced invasions from Alexander the Great, who defeated Darius at the Battle of Issus in 333 BCE and took Babylon in 331 BCE, ending Achaemenid rule.
historical_references.context: Achaemenid Empire, Persia, Greece, Alexander the Great
